traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and technical requirements in docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md are implemented and validated by passing tests.
Specifically: - `@supports story-path REQ-ID...` format is parsed and validated at the syntax level (valid-annotation-format + valid-implements-utils) and at the deep requirement level (valid-req-reference-helpers), including appropriate error messages that mention the concrete storyPath and reqId when validation fails. - Deep validation confirms that each requirement in an @supports line exists in the referenced story file, and multi-story scenarios with shared requirement IDs are supported by scoping IDs per story file. - Core rules `require-story-annotation` and `require-req-annotation` treat @supports as satisfying their respective presence checks, while keeping legacy @story and @req behavior unchanged and well-tested. - Mixed usage of @story, @req, and @supports in the same comment and across codebases is explicitly supported and covered by tests. - Error messages for missing or invalid requirements include storyPath context, satisfying the error-context requirement and user-facing acceptance criteria. - User documentation (API Reference, Migration Guide, README) describes @supports, multi-story behavior, and migration patterns, satisfying the documentation acceptance criterion.
Given the comprehensive test coverage tied directly to this story file and the implementation details above, this story is fully implemented and passes.
